title: Algebraic rational functions from finite global sections of a normal scheme
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative integral domain, put $F=\operatorname{Frac}A$, and let $h:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a dominant morphism from an integral scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Assume that every local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Put $E=k(X)=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$, where $\eta$ is the generic point [def-sc-function-field], and $R=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Regard $A\subseteq R\subseteq E$ through pullback and the germ at $\eta$, and regard $F\subseteq E$ through the induced fraction-field embedding [def-sfb-dominant-function-field-map]. Suppose $R$ is a finite $A$-module, meaning finitely generated as an $A$-module. Then, inside $E$, the field $L=\operatorname{Frac}R$ satisfies
$$L=\{a\in E:a\text{ is algebraic over }F\}.$$
This is the relative algebraic closure of [def-weil-relative-algebraic-closure]. Moreover $L/F$ is finite, and $L$ is algebraically closed in $E$: every element of $E$ algebraic over $L$ belongs to $L$. For every $a\in E$ algebraic over $F$, there exist $0\ne d\in A$ and $r\in R$ with $r=da$ in $E$ (so $a=r/d$). Algebraicity has the meaning of [def-weil-algebraic-element]. Neither properness nor a finite-type hypothesis is imposed on $h$; finiteness of $R$ is the stated module hypothesis.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field], the generic germ embeds $R$ into the field $E$, so $R$ is a domain. With the stipulated injective map $A\subseteq R$, [lem-trf-finite-domain-fraction-degree] gives $[L:F]<\infty$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] to the finite $F$-module $L$: each element of $L$ satisfies a monic (hence nonzero) polynomial over $F$, and so is algebraic over $F$. Its equality in $E$ is the same polynomial equality, since the embedding of $L$ extends that of $R$.

proof.text:

e0$, and set $d=\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}v_i
e0$. Thus $dc_i=u_i\prod_{j
e i}v_j\in A$. Put $b=da$. Multiplying the equation by $d^n$ gives $b^n+\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}e_i b^i=0$, where $e_i=d^{n-i}c_i=d^{n-i-1}(dc_i)\in A$. This is a monic equation for $b$ over $A$.

source.place: Tag 0358 (lemma-normal-integral-sections), adapted monic-equation argument; explicit denominator calculation

proof.text: For each $x\in X$, [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] identifies $E$ with the fraction field of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ via the compatible map $\rho_x$. Send the coefficients $e_i$ of step 2 through $A\to R\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Their images in $E$ are unchanged, since all maps are pullbacks and germs of the same sections. Consequently $b$ satisfies the same monic equation over $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. This local ring is integrally closed by hypothesis, so the definition [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] puts $b$ in $\rho_x(\mathcal O_{X,x})$.

source.place: Tag 0358 (lemma-normal-integral-sections), local integrally closed domain argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-function-field-sections-glue] with the nonempty open $U=X$ and $g=b$. Step 3 verifies its local membership hypothesis at every point. It gives $r\in R$ whose generic germ is $b=da$. Therefore $a=r/d\in L$, because $d\in A\subseteq R$ is nonzero. This also proves the specified denominator conclusion with its nonzero denominator in $A$.

source.place: Tag 0358 (lemma-normal-integral-sections), local representatives glue; use the existing general gluing theorem

proof.text: Step 1 gives $L\subseteq\{a\in E:a\text{ algebraic over }F\}$, and steps 2--4 give the reverse inclusion. The resulting set is exactly the relative algebraic closure by [def-weil-relative-algebraic-closure]. Finiteness of $L/F$ was already proved in step 1.

source.place: Tag 09GI (lemma-algebraic-elements), identification with the relative algebraic closure

proof.text: If $a\in E$ is algebraic over $L$, step 1 says that $L/F$ is algebraic. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-element-tower] to the compatible tower $F\subseteq L\subseteq E$. It makes $a$ algebraic over $F$, and the equality of step 5 then gives $a\in L$. This is the asserted algebraic closedness of $L$ inside $E$.

Step 2: I checked the denominator computation e_i=d^{n-i-1}(d c_i) with n>=1; it is elementary. Step 3: the coefficients are germs of the same sections, and the normal-ring definition is applied via clause 2 of the stalk lemma. Step 4: function-field-sections-glue with U=X gives r=da, which also proves the denominator clause. Step 5 uses the definition of the relative algebraic closure. Step 6 applies the new leaf to F in L in E. proof_deps equals the union of the uses.
